children: The TAIEX, Taiwan’s benchmark stock index, rose 355 points, or 0.7%, to 48,255 in Wednesday morning trading, gaining for the sixth straight session and hitting a record high, mainly buoyed by gains in electronic technology amid optimism over AI infrastructure investment.
The index surpassed the 48,000 mark for the third time intraday.
Electronic technology advanced 1.2%, with TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker and accounting for more than 40% of the market's total value, climbing 1.2% after falling on Tuesday.
Meanwhile, Nanya Technology and Asia Vital Component surged by 5.0% and 4.1%, respectively.
The broader index rose after the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite on Wall Street hit a record high, buoyed by solid gains in AI-related companies.
Further easing in oil prices and US Treasury yields also fueled sentiment.
Optimism over the Trump-Xi summit this week also fueled sentiment, as AI and tariffs are expected to be discussed at the meeting.

title: Taiwan Stocks Hit Record High as Tech Stocks Rally
